answer.entry: Dried laver (hoshi-nori) MEXT 09003, Japanese Standard Tables 2020 8th ed.

7.source: https://eat-treat.jp/food2021s/1125 (hoshi-nori) and /1126 (yaki-nori), mirrors of MEXT Standard Tables of Food Composition 2020 8th rev.; https://patient.info/nutrition/foods/seaweed-nori-dried-raw (CoFID 2021); https://www.matvaretabellen.no/en/nori-seaweed-dried ; https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/Iodine-HealthProfessional/
7.notes: Current DB row (35 kcal) is USDA Seaweed, laver, raw. Mirror site eat-treat.jp not the official MEXT PDF (couldn't extract rows from the PDF). Vitamin values in MEXT are very high vs USDA raw; K 2600 mcg and folate 1200 are as listed. Retail sushi nori is closest to yaki-nori (09004) if toasted; hoshi-nori is the untoasted dried sheet. Iodine in nori varies up to ~4x between sources (Norway 6367 is an unpublished 2025 analysis, outlier).

answer.iodine_mcg_per_g_ODS: about 45 (label); 78 mcg per 1/4 tsp implies ~1.5 g salt = ~52 mcg/g

8.notes: ODS: iodized salt 1/4 tsp = 78 mcg iodine (52% DV); label on US iodized salt is 45 mcg/g, measured samples average 47.5-50.7 mcg/g. ODS gives no gram weight for 1/4 tsp on the page I read. Use ~45-50 mcg/g.
